1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You draw on innate magic to cast Sorcerer spells.

Cantrips. You know four Sorcerer cantrips of your choice (Light, Prestidigitation, Shocking Grasp, and Sorcerous Burst are recommended). Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Sorcerer cantrip. At levels 4 and 10, you learn one additional Sorcerer cantrip, as shown in the class table.

Spell Slots. The Sorcerer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Sorcerer spells of level 1+ that you can cast. To start, choose two level 1 spells (Burning Hands and Detect Magic are recommended). Your number of prepared spells increases as you gain levels, as shown in the class table, and the spells must be of levels for which you have spell slots.
If another Sorcerer feature gives you spells that are always prepared, they don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare, but they count as Sorcerer spells for you.

Changing Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one prepared spell with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for Sorcerer spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Sorcerer spells.

1.name: Innate Sorcery
1.notes:
Your body holds simmering arcane power. As a Bonus Action, you can unleash this power for 1 minute, gaining the following benefits:
• Your Sorcerer spell save DC increases by 1.
• You have Advantage on attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast.

You can use this feature twice, regaining all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

2.name: Font of Magic
2.notes:
You have a wellspring of magic represented by Sorcery Points, which fuel certain magical effects.

You have 2 Sorcery Points at this level, and you gain more as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the class table. You can’t have more points than the amount listed for your level, and you regain all expended points when you finish a Long Rest.

You can use Sorcery Points for options like converting slots and Metamagic:
• Converting Spell Slots to Sorcery Points. You can expend a spell slot (no action required) to gain Sorcery Points equal to the slot’s level.
• Creating Spell Slots. As a Bonus Action, you can transform Sorcery Points into a spell slot. The Creating Spell Slots table (see creating_spell_slots_table) shows the Sorcery Point cost and minimum Sorcerer level for each slot level (up to level 5). Any slot created this way vanishes when you finish a Long Rest.

2.name: Metamagic
2.notes:
Your inner magic lets you twist spells to suit your needs. You gain two Metamagic options of your choice from metamagic_options. You use these options to modify spells you cast by spending Sorcery Points.

You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless a Metamagic option specifically allows otherwise.

Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one Metamagic option you know with a different one. You gain two additional options at level 10 and two more at level 17.

3.name: Subclass Feature
3.notes:
You choose a Sorcerer subclass and gain its level 3 feature. You gain additional subclass features at higher Sorcerer levels.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
4.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Sorcerer levels 8, 12, and 16.

5.name: Sorcerous Restoration
5.notes: When you finish a Short Rest, you can regain expended Sorcery Points up to an amount equal to half your Sorcerer level (round down). Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

6.name: Subclass Feature
6.notes:
You gain a level 6 feature from your Sorcerer subclass.

7.name: Sorcery Incarnate
7.notes:
If you have no uses of Innate Sorcery left, you can still activate it by spending 2 Sorcery Points when you take the Bonus Action to do so.

In addition, while Innate Sorcery is active, you can apply up to two Metamagic options to each spell you cast.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
8.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

10.name: Metamagic
10.notes:
You gain two additional Metamagic options of your choice from metamagic_options.

You can still apply only one Metamagic option to a spell when you cast it, unless otherwise noted in an option. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one Metamagic option you know with a different one.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
12.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

19.name: Epic Boon
19.notes: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Dimensional Travel is recommended.

20.name: Arcane Apotheosis
20.notes: While Innate Sorcery is active, you can apply one Metamagic option on each of your turns without spending Sorcery Points on that option.

metamagic_options.name: Careful Spell
metamagic_options.notes: When you cast a spell that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can choose a number of those creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saves against the spell and take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a success.

metamagic_options.name: Distant Spell
metamagic_options.notes: When you cast a spell with a range of at least 5 feet, you can double its range. When you cast a spell with a range of Touch, you can instead make its range 30 feet.

metamagic_options.name: Empowered Spell
metamagic_options.notes: When you roll damage for a spell, you can reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1), and you must use the new rolls. You can use this option even if you have already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

metamagic_options.name: Extended Spell
metamagic_options.notes: When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can double its duration to a maximum of 24 hours. If the spell requires Concentration, you have Advantage on saving throws made to maintain that Concentration.

metamagic_options.name: Heightened Spell
metamagic_options.notes: When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can give one target Disadvantage on its saving throws against the spell.

metamagic_options.name: Quickened Spell
metamagic_options.notes: When you cast a spell with a casting time of an action, you can change its casting time to a Bonus Action for this casting. You can’t modify a spell this way if you have already cast a level 1+ spell on the current turn, nor can you cast a level 1+ spell later in the turn after doing so.

metamagic_options.name: Seeking Spell
metamagic_options.notes: If you make an attack roll for a spell and miss, you can reroll the d20 and must use the new roll. You can use this option even if you have already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

metamagic_options.name: Subtle Spell
metamagic_options.notes: When you cast a spell, you can cast it without any Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components. Material components that are consumed or have a gold cost are still required.

metamagic_options.name: Transmuted Spell
metamagic_options.notes: When you cast a spell that deals Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder damage, you can change its damage type to a different one from that list.

metamagic_options.name: Twinned Spell
metamagic_options.notes: When you cast a spell that can be cast with a higher-level slot to target an additional creature (such as Charm Person), you can increase the spell’s effective level by 1 for that casting by spending 1 Sorcery Point.
